original_title: Everything looks sticky and nobody says "vampire" in the trailer for Disney+ and Hulu's City Of Blood

en.title: City of Blood Trailer Drops: Is This Berlin's Most Brutal Vampire Secret?
en.summary: A new trailer for the German-language series City of Blood has arrived, hinting at a chillingly dystopian Berlin where vampires secretly rule. The series promises a gritty take on immortal creatures, focusing on two sisters caught in the crossfire.
en.body:
Forget fangs and capes; the trailer for **City of Blood** suggests a far more insidious kind of vampirism is at play. This upcoming German import, set to premiere on Disney+ and Hulu, plunges viewers into a Berlin where the elite are literally feeding off the city's lifeblood, all while the word "vampire" remains conspicuously absent. The visuals promise a slick, sticky, and deeply unsettling urban landscape, hinting that survival in this Dracula-infested metropolis will be a messy affair.

Based on the graphic novel **Berlinoir** by Reinhard Kleist and Tobias O. Meissner, **City of Blood** centers on two sisters, Bea and Phoebe, who must navigate this treacherous world. Their logline states they "Uncover a terrifying truth: Vampires control Berlin." The trailer offers glimpses of a climate-controlled dome that might be shielding the city—and its undead rulers—from the sun, a clever nod to the genre's lore. The show doesn't shy away from its metaphors, depicting the sisters needing to "deal blood" to survive while the one-percenters indulge in their sanguinary habits. It’s a bold premise that positions the series as more than just a monster flick, but a commentary on power structures and societal decay.

## A City Under a Bloody Thumb

The eight-episode series, produced by Amusement Park Film and executive produced by **Daniel Brühl**, among others, seems poised to deliver a sophisticated, politically charged narrative. The decision to set the story in Berlin, a city with its own complex history, adds another layer of intrigue. The trailer's aesthetic, described as "sticky" by early viewers, suggests a tangible, grimy atmosphere that contrasts sharply with the opulent, blood-drenched world of the vampire elite. This dichotomy is likely to be central to the show's appeal, offering a visually striking and thematically rich experience for fans who appreciate genre storytelling with a bite.

## What Fans Can Expect

The marketing for **City of Blood** provocatively asks, "Who is the greater monster, human or vampire?" a question that has fueled countless monster narratives but feels particularly relevant given the show's apparent focus on societal critique. For fans of shows like **The Walking Dead** or other "socially conscious monster" series, this premise offers a fresh, European perspective on familiar themes. The placement on both Disney+ and Hulu indicates a broad reach, aiming to capture a global audience hungry for intelligent, genre-bending dramas. The series is set to debut on September 16th, 2026, making it a highly anticipated release for those seeking a darker, more nuanced take on vampire lore.

## What's Next

With the trailer now released, anticipation is building for the full series premiere on September 16th, 2026. Viewers can expect to see how Bea and Phoebe's struggle unfolds as they uncover the dark secrets of Berlin's immortal rulers.

content_raw: You will, we hope, understand implicitly what it means when we say Hulu and Disney+’s new German import series City Of Blood is the kind of vampire show where nobody says “vampire” in the trailer—instead letting the understanding that you’re watching A Very Serious Show that just happens to be about immortal bloodsuckers soak in via osmosis. Still, credit where it’s due: A whole city of blood sounds like it’d end up being exceptionally sticky, and the show’s new trailer depicts Dracula-infested Berlin as a place where you wouldn’t necessarily want to sit down anywhere while wearing a new pair of white pants. Based off Reinhard Kleist and Tobias O. Meissner’s graphic novel Berlinoir , the series stars Lea Drinda and Soma Pysall as two sisters who (per its logline) “Uncover a terrifying truth: Vampires control Berlin.” (We have to assume that the giant climate-controlled dome over the city, which apparently also blocks the vamp-frying parts of sunlight, may have been a major clue.) The show clearly isn’t too worried about making its metaphors subtle, either, as the sisters must apparently “deal blood” to make ends meet, while we see high-powered one percenter types with copious amounts of The Sanguine Stuff dripping down their chins. (Meanwhile, the marketing copy for the show reads like it comes from its own alternate universe, one where audiences have never seen a single episode of The Walking Dead  or literally any other socially conscious monster show ever made, asking: “Who is the greater monster, human or vampire?​”) (It’s the vampires!) City Of Blood  feels like a weird placement for Disney+, presumably as a symptom of the streamer’s ongoing efforts to merge itself with Hulu. (It’ll end up sitting on the service alongside shows like FX’s  The Strain . Also  Bluey , but that’s obviously unrelated.) The series is set to debut on both Disney+ and Hulu on September 16.
